To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the BRCA1, BRCA2 and the AR genes are involved in hereditary breast cancer, whereas the TP53 and AT genes appear to be involved in breast cancer in the context of other malignancies.

the breast cancer susceptibility genes are located at the following chromosomal locations and have the following functions: 17q21 (BRCA1) - tumor suppressor gene; 13q12-13 (BRCA2) - tumor suppressors gene; 17p13.3 (TP53) - tumor suppressive gene; Xq11-13 (AR) - androgen receptor gene, and 11q22-23 (AT) - gene for DNA repair.
the BRCA1 gene is involved in the majority of the breast cancer families with both male (BRCA1) and female (BRCA1 and BRCA2) breast cancer cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the genetic heterogeneity in breast-ovarian and male breast cancer susceptibility.
elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of hereditary breast cancer, in order to develop strategies for the early detection and prevention of breast cancer.
the genetic basis of breast cancer susceptibility, with a particular focus on the role of the BRCA2 and AR genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the genetic heterogeneity in breast and/or breast and ovarian cancer susceptibility can be explained by germ-line mutations in BRCA1, BRCA2, TP53, AR and AT genes, but not by mutations in other genes.

germ-line mutations of the BRCA1, BRCA2, and TP53 genes are involved in a large proportion of the breast cancer families, whereas mutations in the AR and AT genes are involved in only a few families with breast cancer.
at least 50% of the breast cancer cases with a family history of breast cancer are caused by germ-line mutations in one of these five genes or gene regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic basis of breast cancer is complex and involves a variety of different genetic alterations.
the BRCA1 and BRCA2 loci account for the majority of the autosomal dominant susceptibility, but that other genes are involved as well.

germ-line mutations are involved in 60-70% of breast cancer families, whereas in the remaining 30-40% of breast cancer cases the disease is caused by environmental factors and/or genetic polymorphisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic heterogeneity of breast cancer susceptibility is large, and the genes and gene regions that confer susceptibility to breast, ovarian, and male breast cancer are different.

breast cancer is a genetically heterogeneous disease, which may be caused by a number of different genes and gene regions, and that these genes and gene regions may also be involved in other types of cancer.

the majority of the families with breast cancer have mutations in BRCA1, BRCA2 or AT, and that the remaining families are likely to be caused by mutations in as yet unidentified genes or gene regions.
